title: Latency Sankey: trace-to-metrics path for streaming vs blocking by model/route
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an interactive Sankey-style dashboard that ties distributed trace spans to metric rollups and logs so engineers can quickly see where latency is spent across model versions and routes, with explicit streaming vs non-streaming breakdowns at p50/p95/p99. The dashboard should surface connector points between the traces (span-level durations), metric aggregates (token-generation time, decode time, network time), and log-derived errors (e.g., grpc timeouts, backpressure). Primary goal: accelerate RCA for tail latency regressions and provide actionable knobs for routing/batching/quantization tuning.
acceptance_criteria: Sankey view exists for a selectable time window (15m / 1h / 24h) showing major latency contributors with edge widths proportional to aggregate latency at p50/p95/p99
Toggle to compare streaming vs non-streaming I/O modes and highlight top-3 divergent components per model/route
Trace links from each Sankey node open into the trace viewer with pre-applied filters (model, route, request_id) for sample spans
Backend metric queries are performant (query latency < 2s for 1h window) and use pre-aggregated rollups where possible
Dashboard included in Console under Observability > Latency > Sankey (with perms matching existing dashboards)
Runbook section added describing common remediation actions (increase kv-cache, adjust batching window, fallback model)
tasks: Define and document span-to-metric mapping (trace span names -> metric keys) in Confluence
Add trace hooks to serving runtime to tag spans with model_version, route, io_mode, token_count
Create backend rollup pipeline: hourly and 5m windows for latency percentiles by model+route+io_mode
Design frontend Sankey component and interactions (Figma mock + accessibility review)
Wire up trace links and validate sampling rates do not bias p99 calculations
Add alerting: when p99 of route deviates > 30% vs baseline and streaming/non-streaming delta > 20%
decisions: Use span attribute 'rw.model_version' and 'rw.io_mode' to avoid creating new telemetry keys
Sampling policy: keep current 0.5% base sampling but add target sampling for high-latency traces (adaptive sampling) to ensure p99 visibility
Rollups: 5m for near-real-time, 1h daily retention for historical diffs; full raw spans retained for 7 days for trace lookups
Frontend will compute Sankey edge widths from metric delta (latency_ms * count) instead of raw counts to emphasize time impact
